text: Rousseau's Emile, or On Education was condemned in Paris in 1762. On 9 June 1762 the Parlement de Paris condemned the book to be torn and burned and ordered the arrest of its author, who narrowly escaped arrest when the judgment was executed on 11 June. The government of Geneva also condemned it. The book was banned in Paris and Geneva because of its section titled "Profession of Faith of the Savoyard Vicar", and the Church forbade it and listed it on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum.
